topic: The Birdcage was built to trap Doflamingo's enemies, but it ends up exposing him instead
title: Doflamingo's Birdcage Trapped Himself, Not His Enemies
description: Doflamingo built the Birdcage to trap his enemies on Dressrosa, but it ends up trapping him inside a city that already knows his secret. Here's why his own technique backfires. Was the Birdcage ever really about the enemies, or himself?
comment: Does the Birdcage prove Doflamingo panicked, or was exposing his own lie always the risk he had to take? Pick one.

lines.text: Doflamingo built the Birdcage to trap his enemies. It trapped him instead.

shot.fallback: pirate king summoning a cage of strings

lines.text: He sealed off all of Dressrosa so nobody could leave and no help could get in.

shot.fallback: giant cage of strings around an island

lines.text: So why did his own cage end up proving every lie he'd ever told?
The second it goes up, Doflamingo announces a twisted game to his own citizens.
Take him down, or hand over his enemies for a reward, he tells them.

shot.fallback: wanted posters appearing across a city

lines.text: But most of those citizens just got their memories back from ten years as living toys.
And every one of them now remembers exactly who framed their king.
Fujitora, the Admiral standing right next to him, starts doubting every word Doflamingo says.

shot.fallback: admiral growing suspicious of an ally

lines.text: Sabo fights an Admiral to a standstill just to buy time to reach that palace.

shot.fallback: fighter holding off a powerful admiral

lines.text: The cage built to trap an island ends up trapping only the truth, right next to him.

shot.fallback: tyrant trapped inside his own creation

lines.text: Because Doflamingo built that cage to trap his enemies...

shot.fallback: pirate king summoning a cage of strings

self_check.hook: line 1 states the claim (Birdcage trapping Doflamingo himself) in the first 2 seconds
